items.text: Code trace complete. ComputeRollup (service.go:246-281) has two paths that produce false pending counts: (1) LoadItem errors count as pending (line 262-264), and (2) items with StatusBacklog or StatusReady fall to the default case (line 273-274). The Archived counter (lines 276-278) is tracked separately and does NOT feed into the frontend progress bar — rollupTotal() only sums completed+inProgress+failed+pending. So the double-counting of archived is cosmetic, not the root cause.

The archive handler (backlog/handler.go:421) requires items to be in a terminal state before archiving. However, if an archived item is subsequently deleted from disk, LoadItem fails and ComputeRollup counts it as pending. This is the most likely root cause: the initiative references items that no longer exist on disk.

items.topic: How should ComputeRollup handle archived items?
items.context: Currently, archived items are counted by their backlog status (completed/failed/etc.) AND separately incremented in the Archived counter. The progress bar ignores the Archived counter entirely. If an archived item can't be loaded, it's counted as pending. We need to decide how archived items should participate in the progress calculation.

options.label: Exclude archived items from active status counts entirely
options.rationale: Archived items are 'done' from the user's perspective — they shouldn't affect the progress bar at all. Subtract them from Total and don't count them in any status bucket. Show 'N archived' as a separate label. This is the cleanest UX but changes how Total is interpreted.

options.label: Keep archived items in their status bucket but fix load failures
options.rationale: Only fix the load-failure path — if LoadItem fails, check if the item was archived (e.g., by checking a separate index) and count it as completed instead of pending. Minimal change but doesn't address the conceptual issue of archived items inflating counts.

items.topic: How should load failures (missing items) be counted?
items.context: When LoadItem returns an error for an initiative member (item deleted, renamed, or corrupted on disk), ComputeRollup currently counts it as pending. This silently inflates the pending count for items that may have been completed and then cleaned up. The fix for this is somewhat independent of the archived-items decision.

options.label: Count load failures as completed (assume cleaned up)
options.rationale: Items that can't be loaded were likely completed and archived/deleted. Counting them as completed avoids phantom pending items. Risk: genuinely missing items (e.g., typos in item references) would be hidden.

options.label: Exclude load failures from the count entirely
options.rationale: Don't count items that can't be loaded in any bucket — subtract them from Total. The progress bar only reflects items that actually exist. This is the most accurate representation.

options.label: Keep counting load failures as pending but add a warning
options.rationale: Preserve current behavior but surface a warning in the UI or API response so users know some items couldn't be resolved. Most conservative change.

items.topic: Should the progress bar show an 'archived' segment?
items.context: The frontend progress bar currently shows 4 segments: completed, in progress, failed, pending. If we exclude archived items from the active count (decision d1=A), users might wonder where those items went. Adding an archived segment or label could improve clarity.

options.label: Add an 'archived' label (count only, no bar segment)
options.rationale: Show 'N archived' in the label row below the bar, similar to how 'N total' is shown. Doesn't clutter the bar itself. Simple to implement.

options.label: Add an 'archived' bar segment
options.rationale: Give archived items their own colored segment in the bar. More visual but may add noise for a category users don't actively track.

options.label: No archived indicator — just exclude silently
options.rationale: Keep the progress bar clean. Users can see archived items in the items list if they need to. Simplest change.
